Fear Mongering and Xenophobia

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fight for resources and opportunities, xenophobic attitudes bubbling under, can South Africa curb the next waive of violent attacks

Unique Selling Point:
In a time when the country was engulfed by looting and destruction of retail stores and property, Nhlanhla 'lux' Dlamini emerged as the voice of reason and a leader in the community. Militant and determined to protect one of the largest malls in Soweto, Dlamini rallied communinity members to keep guard at Maponya Mall. 2000 jobs were at stake and potentially millions if the mall were to be vandalised. Celebrated in Soweto and across the country as an inspiring leader, the 33 year old is at the forefront of a new movement. Still militant and always in military garb, Nhlanhla 'lux' Dlamini now leads Operation Dudula, spreading the call to #PutSouthAfricansFirst. The group moves from township to township and areas that have a high immigrant population, calling for undocumented foreigners to return to their home countries and citizens to be given first preference for jobs.


In a climate of rising nationalistic, anti-immigrant rhetoric and hostile attitudes, South Africa is becoming unsafe for many foreign nationals living in the country. In the townships and inner city centres, foreign nationals have blended into pockets of society across the country, working menial jobs or getting by as informal traders. But the message from despondent South Africans who are frustrated by the lack of jobs and resources is clear, go back to your country.

The insert will introduce us to migrants who live and work in South Africa during a time when there are concerted campaigns to make their lives here uncomfortable. The country's woes are well known and well documented, the South African is not capable state and the economy is shrinking. We'll also meet South Africans that are gatvol and are calling for policy changes that will put citizens first for job opportunities etc.



Summary:
South Africa has a shameful past of violent xenophobic attacks. In 2008 the world was stunned when a Mozambican national, who created a life for himself selling blankets was stabbed and later burnt alive. The images of the 'burning man' left a dark stain in the new South Africa, founded on Ubuntu and diversity. It was in 2015 when the xenophobic past reared its head again. This time KwaZulu Natal was the epicenter, the late king had referred to immigrants as fleas, in no time violence was unleashed.

With these events in the not so distant past and South Africa's appetite for violence, the recent anti-immigrant campaigns put the country on the precipice of another waive of xenophobic attacks.

Extra Budget Items:
May need extra budget for security to accompany crew to Hillbrow for links but will probably stick around Braamfontein, which is much safer compared to inner JHB.

Press Release:


Fear Mongering & Xenophobia
In 2008 the world was stunned when a Mozambican national, who created a life for himself selling blankets was stabbed and later burnt alive. The images of the 'burning man' left a dark stain in the new South Africa. It was in 2015 when the xenophobic past reared its head again. This time KwaZulu Natal was the epicenter, the late king had referred to immigrants as fleas, in no time violence was unleashed.
With these events in the not so distant past, recent anti-immigrant campaigns put the country back on the precipice of another wave of xenophobic attacks. A true fight for survival, resources or opportunities or xenophobic hatred bubbling under – can South Africa curb the next wave of violent attacks?
Operation Dudula is spreading the call to #PutSouthAfricansFirst. The group moves from township to township and areas that have a high immigrant population, calling for undocumented foreigners to return to their home countries and citizens to be given first preference for jobs.
In a climate of rising nationalistic, anti-immigrant rhetoric and hostile attitudes, South Africa is becoming unsafe for many foreign nationals living in the country. In townships and city centres, foreign nationals have blended into pockets of society across the country, working menial jobs or getting by as informal traders.
We meet migrants who live and work in South Africa during a time when there are concerted campaigns to make their lives here uncomfortable.


Script:


70 year old Earnest Mbewe is from Malawi. He moved here 5 decades ago, and has built a simple life for himself. He lives in Ramaphosa township, east of Johannesburg.

He considers South Africa home, and has seen the country at its best… and worst.
VO: In 2008 (?) this township erupted into violence. The targets: people like Earnest.

(This VO to come after “...others had guns) Enerst

01;40 they were carrying pangas, sticks and others had guns. (CUT) 01;47 they don’t say anything they just start chacing after people they know to be foreigners.They don’t belong here. 02;02 they hadn’t done anything, they just didn’t want them here. They must go.
VO: By the time the blood-letting subsided _____ people were dead.

(This comes between Earnest’s upsound and Mac’s link)
Mandela Bridge Link
Link 3
This is a migrant city, many who call Johannesburg home come from different parts of the country, the continent and the world. But with growing anti-immigrant rhetoric, this city has become hostile.
In cosmopolitan Hillbrow, in Johannesburg’s inner city, you’ll meet migrants from all over the African continent. Grimy and crime-ridden it may be, but to them, this is home.

That is, until people clad in army camouflage came to deliver a message: you’re no longer welcome!

This is Operation Dudula - meaning to push away (?) It targets foreign nationals, especially those who are undocumented, insisting they go back to their home countries. Drone of JHB CBD - from Speaking To The Dead. 03;36

Busy street in Hillbrow, Econet Sign, Africa Supermarket…Hotel with different flags.


Transition to south african flags in the air, banners, singing on the street.

Mcdonald

05;05 this time around we came very different because operation dudula, it’s high discipline, it’s high moral, we don’t beat anyone, we don’t take your stock and steal it. We don’t do that. What are we asking them , peacefully, they must go back where they come from because they are illegal in this country. They are causing a problem in this country.
Operation Dudula is steadily gaining ground in the townships and pockets of Johannesburg. The modus operandi? Going door to door to evict foreign nationals without papers.

In this video, you’re seeing a family left in the streets after a so-called clean up operation in Orange Grove on the city’s outskirts.

But, last weekend there was a gear shift: in their biggest operation yet, Dudula enforcers poured into Hillbrow. But, they hadn’t secured a permit to either march or enter the buildings… (first upsound)








Supplied Video





And, at the forefront of the stand-off with the police was this man, the campaign’s leader, Nhlanhla Dlamini.

(This VO to follow “a permit to be in these buildings)




Nhlanhla
00;48 we’ve heard that police are here to make sure that we don’t enter buildings becomes we don’t have a permits. My question is what illegal foreigner has a permit to be in these buildings.










00;56 if south africans are questioned about permits, that means there’s a problem with our law.

If his name sounds familiar, it’s because Nhlanhla was at the forefront of another, very different campaign. In July last year he was pivotal in protecting Soweto’s Maponya Mall from the looting that engulfed Gauteng and KZN.

Now, as convenor of Operation Dudula, he defends his organisation’s tactics, saying they’re in the interests of South African citizens.

Researcher and Analyst, Angelo Fick, has a very different view.






















Angelo
1;06;24- 1;07;07
if people are going around asking people to prove that they are south African, by asking them to present their paperwork who knows what form this will take, it echoes apartheid south African habbits. Where the South African police, the apartheid police would go knocking on people’s doors asking them to prove that they have the right to be in the city. And shouldn’t be endorsed out to the Transkei or baphutatswana or venda. And that’s tragic because one has to think what do these people have in their heads will happen when a person says I’m actually from Malawi.
And adults aren’t the only victims; young people too are often caught up in the chaos



1;07;29
What are we willing to subject people’s children to as we do these house to house searches. 1;07;48 The ugly history in the world is this was done to children in the holocaust, the German police, they ddin’t care that people’s children would be traumatized by this. 01;08;01
Far from being swayed by his critics, Nhlanhla is on a mission: he wants our labour laws to limit the rights of foreigners to work. His rallying cry is “Put South Africans First”
Nhlanhla

2;44 we say, it’s simple in everything that we do big or small you put south africans first everyone else follow. When you talk about the jobs, the low end of the economy, the low hanging fruit of the economy, being the jobs that require no skill. Those jobs belong to South Africans no negotiation,


03;37 and once we achieve that mission of the low hanging fruit we are going to the bigger mission, discussing the land, the banks, we can’t be scared of white people. The are white people who aren’t south africans, even in the white community there are illegal foreigners but we know where are going, it’s just that it looks like this fight is against African foreigners. 03;57 when it’s not true, it’s just that African foreginers are within our proximity when we start to cleaning our country but it’s not limited to them. We are coming to the china mall’s, we are coming to the oriental plazas, to the sandton cities. There are many people that are there that do not have legitimate paper work, wheather for business or personal this country will be clean.
The language around the campaign is explicit.

Perhaps its underlying xenophobia is being fueled by the anti-immigrant rhetoric associated with some politicans. Those making misleading claims, about the number of undocumented migrants in the country and their impact on the economy.

Kate Wilkinson is deputy editor at fact checking NGO, Africa Check (is that the right description?)
































Kate
02;22 - 03;26
One broad category that we see are wildly inflated numbers being shared about the numbers of migrants being shared in the country (CUT). One person who’s been responsible for this is former mayor of johannesburg herman mashaba, who claimed there are 15 million undocumented migrants in the country…he back tracked but in that instance the damage is already don e, you can’t take them from people’s minds and how they influence people in the future.’

08;23
Another statement made by herman mashaba was that 80 percent of inner city residents in Johannesburg were undocumented foreigners… we have data to dispute that, if check it they put the number at around 26 percent.
With South Africa prone to violent xenophobic attacks, claims like these might have severe consequences.




Nhlanhla
04;33 no no the violence was incited long before, when our own government and our law enforcement allowed the country to be like this that was the incitement of violence. All we are doing we are standing up for our own country and putting south africans first and if that is called inciting violence we are prepared to fight and go to jail for that action, not a problem, not a problem at all.
Strong words that have a particular resonance on the streets of Rampahosa township.It was here 14 years ago that Mozambican, Ernesto Nhamve, was burnt alive. One of dozens of victims of that period’s xenophobic attacks he became their tragic symbol.



No one was ever charged for his murder.
Ramaphosa Link

Ernesto Nhamuave created a life for himself selling blankets, he was a part of this community. It was around here, where after he was beaten and stabbed multiple times, they wrapped him in one of his blankets and set him alight.
Beyond the graffiti, there’s nothing here to mark the horrors of May 2008. All the more troubling when you consider Rampahosa township was at the center of the violence that claimed more than 60 lives nationally - both foreign and South African.

It’s also home to Ernest Mbewe, and where he watched in horror as foreigners were hunted down. a
Earnest
01;34 when I heard that they’d burnt a man, I was heart broken, because we all belong to God, so if you’re going to burn a person, a fellow human being, that’s very sad. Something like that shouldn’t be easy because that’s a soul, it was very sad. I couldn’t even sleep, I’d just see blood and his body burning, very very sad. What happened here in Ramaphosa was devastating.
02;26 you see around that time, life was different, people were traumatized. And many people didn’t like what happened, the mob tried to spread attacks again and people stopped them because the people who died were not just foreigners. Joburg people also died.


LINK

Rising unemployment, a shrinking economy, opportunities are hard to come by. People are frustrated, disillusioned and poor. For many, everyday is a fight for resources and survival.
It’s a recipe for chaos, particularly for those looking for scapegoats to explain the country’s failures. And why it’s in the townships and informal settlements that xenophobic attitudes spill over into violence.



.











MAC Question
03;44 - 04;20
If you’ve lived in South Africa, if you know South Africa. You know that we have almost seasonal outbreak of xenophobic sentiment, xenophobic violence and once one happens we know that in couple of year, in couple of months we have one coming. And i think it emphasise how careful one has to be all the time about migrants in the country. Because that sentiments aren’t just in our past, that sentiment is in our present and it is ready to be enflamed and we need to be careful about the words that we use especially by people in powerful positions.






That’s advice Nhlanhla would do well to heed”

----- more upsound (briefer, though) -------

VO “because it’s clear his words are resonating with his devotees. NHLANHLA
HIGH MORAL HIGH DISCIPLINE






NHLANHLA
HIGH MORAL HIGH DISCIPLINE


Mac 22;46 - 23;04 The question is though, we have this great lexicon in South Africa, Ubuntu, the question then is why does this negative rhetoric resonate with us, this is who we are as a people…

Angelo
24; 47 Ubuntu I think is a very nice myth that south africans tell themselves but it doesn’t work itse;f out in practice necessarily cause if we did have ubuntu we wouldn’t live in a femicidile country. We wouldn’t have the stastics of people dying in police custody, we wouldn’t have the kidnapping and deaths of children, the very notion of micheal khomaphe drowning in a pit latrine toilet wouldn’t have happened, Marikana wouldn’t have happened, the life esidimeni scandal tragedy wouldn’t have happened, so ubuntu is a nice story we tell ourselves

1;19;28 As south africans our obligation is to speak up against these violations whether they are internal, external, whether they happen to people who are considered insiders or outsiders, and here the test will be how do we know that all the people who are targeted are going to be not South African.









11SEC PROMO
They are taking our jobs, they commit crime, they must go back to their countries. These are sentiments commonly heard on South African streets. Why does xenophobic rhetoric spread so easily in the country.
21 SEC PROMO
VO Upsound

we don’t take your stock and steal it. We don’t do that. What are we asking them , peacefully, they must go back where they come from because they are illegal in this country. They are causing a problem in this country.
Are South Africans dissillusioned or are they xenophobic. A new movement is on the rise in parts of Johannesburg and its message is clear - You are no longer welcome

21 SEC PROMO
A new grassroots movement is proposing a new solution for the country’s unemployment problems. Remove all the foreign nationals from restaurants and informal sector and give those jobs to South Africans
Nhlanhla

When you talk about the jobs, the low end of the economy, the low hanging fruit of the economy, being the jobs that require no skill. Those jobs belong to South Africans no negotiation,

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A fight for resources and opportunities, xenophobic attitudes bubbling under, can South Africa curb the next waive of violent attacks
metadata.Unique Selling Point: In a time when the country was engulfed by looting and destruction of retail stores and property, Nhlanhla 'lux' Dlamini emerged as the voice of reason and a leader in the community. Militant and determined to protect one of the largest malls in Soweto, Dlamini rallied communinity members to keep guard at Maponya Mall. 2000 jobs were at stake and potentially millions if the mall were to be vandalised. Celebrated in Soweto and across the country as an inspiring leader, the 33 year old is at the forefront of a new movement. Still militant and always in military garb, Nhlanhla 'lux' Dlamini now leads Operation Dudula, spreading the call to #PutSouthAfricansFirst. The group moves from township to township and areas that have a high immigrant population, calling for undocumented foreigners to return to their home countries and citizens to be given first preference for jobs. In a climate of rising nationalistic, anti-immigrant rhetoric and hostile attitudes, South Africa is becoming unsafe for many foreign nationals living in the country. In the townships and inner city centres, foreign nationals have blended into pockets of society across the country, working menial jobs or getting by as informal traders. But the message from despondent South Africans who are frustrated by the lack of jobs and resources is clear, go back to your country. The insert will introduce us to migrants who live and work in South Africa during a time when there are concerted campaigns to make their lives here uncomfortable. The country's woes are well known and well documented, the South African is not capable state and the economy is shrinking. We'll also meet South Africans that are gatvol and are calling for policy changes that will put citizens first for job opportunities etc.
metadata.Summary: South Africa has a shameful past of violent xenophobic attacks. In 2008 the world was stunned when a Mozambican national, who created a life for himself selling blankets was stabbed and later burnt alive. The images of the 'burning man' left a dark stain in the new South Africa, founded on Ubuntu and diversity. It was in 2015 when the xenophobic past reared its head again. This time KwaZulu Natal was the epicenter, the late king had referred to immigrants as fleas, in no time violence was unleashed. With these events in the not so distant past and South Africa's appetite for violence, the recent anti-immigrant campaigns put the country on the precipice of another waive of xenophobic attacks.
